---
name: slack-api
description: Work with the Slack Web API to post messages and Block Kit rich messages, reply in threads, update and delete messages, list and read channels, conversations, and DMs, fetch user info, search messages, manage reactions, and schedule sends. Use when a task involves Slack notifications, reading Slack workspace data, or building Slack API integrations against api.slack.com.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Perform Slack operations directly against the Web API at `https://slack.com/api` using any HTTP client (`curl`, Python `requests`, Node `fetch`). Every endpoint returns JSON with an `ok` field: `true` on success, `false` with an `error` string otherwise. No Slack SDK is required.

## Authenticate

1. Obtain a token: bot token (`xoxb-...`, preferred) or user token (`xoxp-...`).
2. Read it from the environment (`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`); never hard-code or print tokens.
3. Send the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request.
4. Ensure the app has the scopes required by the endpoint; a token lacking a scope fails with `missing_scope` or `not_allowed_token_type`.

Common bot scopes: `chat:write`, `chat:write.public`, `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `groups:read`, `groups:history`, `im:read`, `im:history`, `users:read`, `users:read.email`, `reactions:write`, `search:read`, `team:read`.

Base request pattern:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://slack.com/api/<method>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '<json body>'
```

Most methods also accept `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies.

## Understand the API

- **Resolve addresses.** Channel names change and are not unique; prefer stable IDs such as `C123456`. Look names up with `conversations.list`, then use the returned `id`.
- **Targets.** `channel` accepts a channel ID (`C...`), a user ID for a DM (`U...`, which opens/uses a DM), or sometimes `#name`.
- **Timestamps.** Message `ts` values are strings, not numbers; use them as-is for threading, editing, and deleting.
- **Formatting.** Slack uses mrkdwn, not full Markdown: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `<https://example.com|link text>`, `<@U123>`, `#channel`, `:emoji:`. Use blocks for layout.
- **Pagination.** List-style endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor` until it is empty.
- **Errors.** Business failures return HTTP 200 with `"ok": false`; honor HTTP 429 (`rate_limited`, use the `Retry-After` header) and retry 5xx responses with backoff.

## Post a message

POST `chat.postMessage` with `channel` and either `text`, `blocks`, or both (`text` also serves as the accessible fallback for rich messages).

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "channel": "C123456789",
    "text": "Deploy finished: *api-v2.4.1* is live",
    "link_names": true,
    "unfurl_links": false
  }'
```

The response contains `channel` and `ts`; keep `ts` to reply, edit, or delete later.

Useful `chat.postMessage` options: `thread_ts` (reply in a thread), `mrkdwn` (default true), `username` and `icon_emoji` (when configured for the app), `reply_broadcast` (broadcast a threaded reply to the channel), and `unfurl_links`/`unfurl_media`.

## Send Block Kit messages

Send `blocks` as a JSON array for rich, structured messages. Common block types:

- `header` – bold plain `text` up to 150 characters.
- `section` – `text` (mrkdwn or plain) and optional `fields` (array of text objects, up to 10).
- `divider` – empty object `{ "type": "divider" }`.
- `actions` – interactive `elements` (buttons, select menus) with `action_id` values you define.
- `context` – small `elements` (text or image) for footnotes.
- `image` – `image_url`, `alt_text`, optional `title`.
- `input` – label plus an element (usable in modals).

```json
{
  "channel": "C123456789",
  "text": "Quarterly review is ready",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Q3 Review" } },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Revenue is *up 12%*. <https://example.com/report|Open the full report>" },
      "fields": [
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Revenue:*\n$1.24M" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Customers:*\n3,102" }
      ]
    },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Approve" }, "style": "primary", "action_id": "approve_report" },
        { "type": "button", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Reject" }, "style": "danger", "action_id": "reject_report" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Reply, update, delete, and schedule messages

- Reply inside a thread: POST `chat.postMessage` with the parent `thread_ts`.
- Edit: POST `chat.update` with `channel`, `ts`, and new `text`/`blocks`.
- Delete: POST `chat.delete` with `channel` and `ts`.
- Ephemeral (visible to one user only): POST `chat.postEphemeral` with `channel` and `user`.
- Schedule: POST `chat.scheduleMessage` with `post_at` (unix seconds, at least ~60 s in the future); manage with `chat.scheduledMessages.list` and `chat.deleteScheduledMessage`.

## List channels and conversations

- POST `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim` (or a subset), `limit` (1–1000, default 100), `exclude_archived=true`, and paginate with `cursor`. Filter client-side by `is_member`, `is_archived`, or `name`.
- Get one conversation: `conversations.info` with `channel`.
- Get members: `conversations.members` (paginate); useful for determining who can be messaged.

## Read channel and thread history

- POST `conversations.history` with `channel`, optional `limit` (max 1000 per call, default 100), and optional `cursor` or `oldest`/`latest` (unix seconds). Responses are newest-first; continue while `has_more` is true using `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
- Read a thread: POST `conversations.replies` with `channel` and `ts` (the parent message timestamp).

History endpoints return messages for the given conversation only; they never span channels.

## Find users and open DMs

- POST `users.list` (paginate with `cursor`) or `users.info` with `user`.
- Find by email: POST `users.lookupByEmail` with `email`.
- Useful fields: `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `is_bot`, `deleted`, `is_owner`.
- Open a DM: POST `conversations.open` with `users` (comma-separated for a group DM), then post to the returned `channel.id`. For one-on-one DMs, `chat.postMessage` with the user ID also works.

## Search messages

- POST `search.messages` with a `query` supporting search syntax such as `from:@alice`, `in:#general`, `has::white_check_mark:`, and quoted phrases.
- Paginate with `count`/`page`, or `cursor` when `sort=timestamp` is used.
- Matches are returned in `messages.matches`, each with `channel`, `ts`, `text`, `user`, and `permalink`; prefer using permalinks over pasting full text.

## Manage reactions

- Add: POST `reactions.add` with `channel`, `name` (emoji name without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), and `timestamp` (the message `ts`).
- Remove: POST `reactions.remove` with the same parameters.
- Get: POST `reactions.get` for one message, or `reactions.list` for a user's recent reactions.

## Handle errors and rate limits

Parse `ok: false` errors and act accordingly:

- `not_authed`, `invalid_auth`, `account_inactive`, `token_revoked` – authentication problem; stop and report.
- `missing_scope`, `not_allowed_token_type` – token lacks the required scope or is the wrong token type.
- `channel_not_found`, `user_not_found`, `is_archived` – bad or archived target.
- `msg_too_long` – text exceeds 40,000 characters.
- `invalid_timestamp` – the `ts` value is malformed or out of range.
- HTTP 429 / `ratelimited` – honor the `Retry-After` header before retrying.
- `internal_error` – transient; retry with exponential backoff.

Rate limits vary per method (tiers 1–4). When fanning out many posts or channel reads, add small delays (roughly 50–100 ms) between calls and watch for 429 responses.

## Guidance for agents

- If the environment provides a registered Slack helper tool, use it for the operation; fall back to these Web API recipes otherwise.
- Never invent tokens or workspace credentials; use provided credentials or ask for them.
- Keep messages concise unless the user requests detail; put long content in a section block or a thread.
- Do not paste full conversation dumps into context; summarize history and search results, quoting exact text only when the user needs it.
